## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
In the edition of V. Fausböll, the Jātaka is positioned as the sixth story of its section, preceding the *Mahāsupinajātaka*, and opens around the canonical verse beginning *Asaṁkiyomhi gāmamhi* ("The village breeds no fear in me") [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877]. The framing narrative is set at Jetavana, where the Buddha recounts the episode concerning a lay follower (*upāsaka*) residing in Sāvatthi who was an earnest stream-enterer (*sotāpanna*); while journeying through a forest with a merchant caravan that had halted to establish a camp, the lay disciple calmly walked up and down at the base of a tree [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877].
In the past-life narrative, the Bodhisatta appears as an ascetic (*tāpaso*) who preaches the Dhamma with the canonical verse to the caravan folk; practicing the four divine abidings (*brahmavihāra*) throughout his life, he attains rebirth in the Brahmā world (*Brahmaloka*) [Fausböll 1877]. In the concluding identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha reveals that the caravan company in that existence was his present assembly, while the ascetic was the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1877]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus reports any internal Pali text-reuse or cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan for this Jātaka [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
